mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best illustrates the irony in Lencho's response after receiving the money from the post office?

options.A: Lencho thanks the postmaster for the full amount he requested.
options.B: Lencho writes to God asking for exactly 1000 rupees, even though he knows the post office employees kept part of the money.
options.C: Lencho blames the postmaster for not sending enough money.
options.D: Lencho decides to plant a different crop after the hailstorm.

mcqs.answer: Lencho writes to God asking for exactly 1000 rupees, even though he knows the post office employees kept part of the money.
mcqs.explanation: The irony lies in Lencho’s unwavering belief that God will send the full amount he needs, despite the fact that the post office employees have already taken a portion of the money. He trusts divine providence over the human reality of the shortfall.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify the central message of the story
mcqs.question: What is the central message conveyed by the story "A Letter to God"?

options.A: Faith in divine providence can sustain a person even in extreme hardship.
options.B: Modern agriculture depends on advanced technology.
options.C: Honesty is the most important virtue in society.
options.D: Nature's power is unpredictable and must be feared.

mcqs.answer: Faith in divine providence can sustain a person even in extreme hardship.
mcqs.explanation: The story emphasizes Lencho’s unshaken faith that God will answer his prayer for rain and money, highlighting the theme that belief in divine help can give hope despite severe adversity.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand Lencho's dependence on his crop
mcqs.question: Why is Lencho's crop so important to him?

options.A: It is a hobby that he enjoys in his free time.
options.B: It is his sole source of livelihood and income for his family.
options.C: It is a gift he received from a neighbor.
options.D: It is used only for decorative purposes.

mcqs.answer: It is his sole source of livelihood and income for his family.
mcqs.explanation: Lencho depends entirely on the harvest to earn money for his family's daily needs; without the crop, he would have no means of support.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the importance of rain to his livelihood
mcqs.question: In the story, why does Lencho consider rain essential?

options.A: Rain makes the soil cooler for planting.
options.B: Rain is needed for his crops to grow, which sustains his family's livelihood.
options.C: Rain helps him wash his clothes more easily.
options.D: Rain attracts birds that protect the fields.

mcqs.answer: Rain is needed for his crops to grow, which sustains his family's livelihood.
mcqs.explanation: Lencho’s entire income depends on a good harvest, and a good harvest is possible only if there is sufficient rain. Hence, rain is directly linked to his survival.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain the destruction caused by the hailstorm
mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the damage caused by the hailstorm on Lencho's farm?

options.A: Only a few leaves were damaged, but the majority of the crop survived.
options.B: The hailstorm destroyed the entire crop, leaving the fields barren.
options.C: The hailstorm damaged the farmhouse but left the crops untouched.
options.D: The hailstorm caused minor soil erosion without affecting the plants.

mcqs.answer: The hailstorm destroyed the entire crop, leaving the fields barren.
mcqs.explanation: The story states that the hailstorm completely ruined Lencho’s crop, wiping out his expected harvest and leaving him with nothing to sell.

mcqs.learning_point: Analyse Lencho's complete faith in God
mcqs.question: How does Lencho's action of writing a letter to God after the hailstorm demonstrate his complete faith?

options.A: He writes a confident request for money, trusting that God will provide it despite the disaster.
options.B: He decides to move to the city and find a different job.
options.C: He blames the government for the lack of rain.
options.D: He stops farming altogether and looks for other sources of income.

mcqs.answer: He writes a confident request for money, trusting that God will provide it despite the disaster.
mcqs.explanation: Lencho’s letter to God, asking for a specific amount of money, shows his absolute belief that divine intervention will solve his problem, reflecting unwavering faith.

mcqs.question: Which example from the story best shows the irony in Lencho's attitude toward the money he receives?

options.A: He thanks the postmaster for the exact amount he asked for.
options.B: He writes to God asking for 1000 rupees, even though he knows the post office employees kept part of the money.
options.C: He decides to plant a different crop after the hailstorm.
options.D: He complains to his neighbors about the weather.

mcqs.answer: He writes to God asking for 1000 rupees, even though he knows the post office employees kept part of the money.
mcqs.explanation: The irony is that Lencho, aware that the post office workers have taken some of the money, still believes God will send the full amount he requested, showing a disconnect between reality and his faith.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify the central message of the story
mcqs.question: If a farmer today faced a similar disaster and wrote a letter to a higher power, what central message from "A Letter to God" would the story convey to him?

options.A: Unwavering faith can persist even in the face of severe adversity.
options.B: Modern technology is the only solution to agricultural problems.
options.C: It is better to rely solely on government aid.
options.D: Changing crops each season guarantees success.

mcqs.answer: Unwavering faith can persist even in the face of severe adversity.
mcqs.explanation: The story’s core message is that Lencho’s steadfast belief in divine help remains intact despite the calamity, illustrating that deep faith can endure extreme hardship.
